Job Description : GET-PQE
Department : Quality
Role : Product Quality Engineer (PQE) to join our Quality Assurance team. In this role, you will be the primary technical owner of product quality, reliability, and compliance from New Product Introduction (NPI) through mass production. You will analyze product defects, drive root-cause investigations for functional or cosmetic failures, and implement robust corrective and preventive actions (CAPA). The ideal candidate possesses deep technical knowledge of electronic assemblies, components, and testing methodologies, alongside the ability to interface effectively with both internal production teams and external customers.
Postion : GET-PQE

Job Description : Key Responsibilities • NPI & Product Launch Quality: Participate in New Product Introduction (NPI) reviews. Review DFMs (Design for Manufacturability) and DFQs (Design for Quality) to establish Quality Control Plans, inspection criteria, and testing gates before mass production. • Failure Analysis & Root Cause Determination: Lead deep-dive failure analysis on complex product defects (e.g., PCBA component failures, solder joint fractures, functional test drops). Use tools like cross-sectioning, microscopy, or X-ray inspection to identify underlying failure mechanisms. • CAPA Management: Drive Internal and Customer Corrective Action Requests (CAR/8D reports). Collaborate with Process Engineering and Production to implement permanent corrective actions and prevent defect recurrence. • Yield & Reliability Optimization: Monitor daily and weekly product yield trends (from SMT AOI to Final Functional Test). Lead yield-improvement projects for underperforming product models. • Customer Quality Interface: Act as the technical point of contact for customer quality issues. Present data-driven failure analysis and engineering reports directly to client quality teams. • Standards & Compliance: Ensure products strictly comply with international electronics quality standards.

KPI : Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Your success in this role will be measured by the following core metrics: 1. Customer Escapes / DPPM: Maintain Customer Defective Parts Per Million (DPPM) below the organizational or client-specified target. 2. 8D / CAR Closure Lead Time: Achieve an average 8D report closure rate within the target window (e.g., 3-day turnaround for containment, 14 days for permanent closure). 3. First Pass Yield (FPY) Improvement: Successfully hit or exceed the product-specific final functional test FPY targets through systematic defect elimination. 4. Repeat Defect Rate: Maintain a 0% recurrence rate for issues that have undergone a formal CAPA closure. 5. Scrap Cost Reduction: Decrease internal product scrap costs resulting from quality defects and poorly executed reworks. Required Qualifications & Skills • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electronics & Communication Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.

Job Description : GET-PQC
Department : Quality
Role : Process Quality Control (PQC) Engineer will be the primary guardian of process stability on the production floor. You will be responsible for implementing, monitoring, and auditing manufacturing checkpoints across SMT, Wave Soldering, manual insertion, and final assembly lines. Your mission is to catch variations early, enforce strict process parameters, and optimize manufacturing control plans so that defects are prevented before they are ever built.
Postion : GET-PQC

Job Description : Key Responsibilities • Line Set-up & First-Piece Approval: Oversee and sign off on "First Piece/First Article Inspection" (FAI) approvals during shift changes, model changeovers, or after equipment maintenance before mass production begins. • Statistical Process Control (SPC): Deploy and manage SPC charts on critical parameters (e.g., solder paste height/volume, reflow oven thermal profiles, wave solder pot temperatures). Analyze trends to identify and correct process drift before it causes defects. • Process Audits: Conduct regular, structured layer process audits (LPA) and 5S/ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) compliance audits across all manufacturing lines. • Defect Containment & MRB: Lead immediate containment actions when a line defect spike occurs. Quarantine suspect materials, issue Material Review Board (MRB) dispositions, and issue internal Corrective Action Requests (CAR) to production teams. • Rework & Repair Governance: Validate that all board reworks and repairs strictly adhere to IPC-7711/7721 standards and that no unauthorized rework methods are used on the floor. • Documentation Control: Maintain and update Quality Control Plans, Inspection Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), visual defect catalogs, and check-sheets at all inspection gates (IQC/IPQC/FQC).

KPI : Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Your success in this role will be measured by the following process-centric metrics: 1. In-Process Defect Rate (PPM / DPMO): Maintain the process Defect Per Million Opportunities (DPMO) or Line PPM below the established organizational plant targets. 2. First-Piece Approval Accuracy: Achieve a 100% success rate on First Article Inspections, ensuring zero line-restarts due to skipped or faulty initial approvals. 3. Out-of-Control Action Plan (OCAP) Response Time: Respond to and contain SPC "out-of-control" triggers or line quality stops within the designated SLA (e.g., under 15 minutes). 4. Audit Compliance Score: Maintain a score of greater than 95% on internal process, ESD, and Quality Control Plan compliance audits. 5. Recurring Process Issues: Maintain a 0% recurrence rate for specific line defects once an internal corrective action has been signed off and implemented. Required Qualifications & Skills • Education: Bachelor’s degree or Diploma in Electronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related industrial technical field.

Job Description : GET-Line Leader
Department : Production
Role : Production Line Leader to oversee daily operations on our electronics manufacturing and assembly lines. In this role, you will be directly responsible for leading a team of operators, technicians, and material handlers to meet daily production targets safely and efficiently. As the frontline leader, you will ensure strict adherence to quality standards, manage line balance, minimize downtime, and foster a culture of continuous improvement.
Postion : GET-Line Leader

Job Description : Key Responsibilities • Daily Execution & Line Balancing: Organize daily line setups, allocate labor efficiently, and maintain proper line balancing to ensure optimal flow across assembly, and test stations. • Team Leadership & Training: Lead daily shift-kickoff meetings (huddles) to communicate targets. Train, cross-train, and mentor operators on standard operating procedures (SOPs) and safety guidelines. • Quality Enforcement: Monitor the line for defects. Ensure adherence to ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) controls, component handling procedures, and quality benchmarks. Pause production if a critical quality deviation occurs. • Downtime Mitigation: Coordinate closely with Maintenance and Process Engineers to quickly troubleshoot equipment bottlenecks (e.g., pick-and-place errors, reflow issues, or tester downtime). • Material & 5S Management: Ensure continuous material availability at the line to prevent stoppages. Maintain strict 5S standards (Sort, Set in order, Shine, Standardize, Sustain) across the entire workstation area. • Data Logging & Reporting: Accurately log hourly output, scrap data, and downtime incidents into the MES (Manufacturing Execution System) or shift logs.

KPI : Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Your success in this role will be measured by the following metrics: 1. Output vs. Target (Plan Attainment): Achieve greater than 95% of the scheduled production volume target per shift. 2. First Pass Yield (FPY): Maintain the line's FPY above the designated benchmark (typically greater than 98% for assembly/test) by minimizing defects like misalignment, poor soldering, or missing components. 3. Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) / Line Efficiency: Maximize line utilization and minimize unplanned downtime to hit shift efficiency targets. 4. Scrap & Material Variance: Keep material scrap rates (e.g., dropped SMT components or damaged PCBs) below the target threshold (e.g., less than 0.5%). 5. 5S & Safety Compliance: Achieve excellent scores on weekly/monthly 5S audits and maintain a zero-accident record on your designated line. Required Qualifications & Skills • Education: High School Diploma or ITI/Diploma in Electronics/Mechanical Engineering (preferred).
